name: Elon Musk
role: Businessman (Tesla, SpaceX, X); led the Department of Government Efficiency (2025); announced the America Party (2025)
summary: A tech entrepreneur who calls himself a free speech absolutist and favors a smaller federal government, zero tariffs and direct democracy, while backing a carbon tax, nuclear power, AI oversight and income payments for those displaced by AI. Since about 2022 he has aligned with the Republican right on immigration, DEI and gender issues, opposed unions, and supported US exit from NATO and the UN. He broke with Trump in 2025 over spending and floated a centrist America Party.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Pushes deregulation and cuts to government, opposes corporate subsidies, though he also backs a carbon tax and AI rules.

public-ownership.rationale: In March 2025 he said 'we should privatize anything that can be privatized', naming the Postal Service and Amtrak, because only firms that can go bankrupt get a feedback loop.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Mixed: he opposes a wealth tax and clashed with Senator Warren over taxing billionaires (Isaacson, chapter 'Politics'), but has backed estate taxes and said he paid the largest US tax bill in 2021.

unions-good.rationale: Record over words: Tesla under Musk refused to sign a collective agreement with Sweden's IF Metall through a long strike (AP, 2023) and, per the NLRB, took illegal anti-union actions against the UAW drive at Fremont (Isaacson, ch. 69 'Politics').

reviewHistory.rationale: Said in December 2023 he disagrees with the idea of unions and in 2018 questioned why workers would pay dues.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Record over words: Tesla under Musk refused to sign a collective agreement with Sweden's IF Metall through a long strike (AP, 2023) and, per the NLRB, took illegal anti-union actions against the UAW drive at Fremont (Isaacson, ch. 69 'Politics').
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mixed: supports AI regulation and compliance with car and rocket rules (Tucker 2023, about 2:19; DealBook 2023, about 58:58), but says overregulation has gone far too far (Rogan #2223, about 2:12:42).

cut-welfare.rationale: Called entitlements, most of federal spending, 'the big one to eliminate', but framed the aim as fraud and waste; also supports basic income, so the answer is contested.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Joe Rogan #2223 (about 47:26-51:05): says the FDA should judge a drug by whether users say it made them better, and calls banning some drugs like censorship, but also says it is a tricky question and describes meth and Adderall harms. Speaker attribution on the cartel remark is unclear. Mixed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Calls himself a free speech absolutist, defined as speech that matches the law, and opposes censorship beyond the law.

state-harmful.rationale: Wants a much smaller government and fewer agencies but led a government body and does not call for abolishing the state.

limit-guns.rationale: After Uvalde backed universal background checks and limits on assault rifle sales, but says the right to bear arms guards against tyranny; not a strict-limit position.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: No stated position found on this statement.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Told an AfD rally in January 2025 that it is good to be proud of German culture and values and not to lose them in a multiculturalism that dilutes everything.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Mixed: defends skilled H-1B migration (while proposing higher minimum salaries and a yearly fee), wants more legal 'hard-working and honest' migrants and freer movement between Europe and North America, but opposes illegal immigration and criticizes 'uncontrolled immigration'.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Replied 'I agree' to a post saying the US should leave NATO and the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Advocated a zero-tariff free trade zone across the Atlantic.

nation-first.rationale: Fox DOGE interview (about 36:27): says a person should put the interests of the United States above those of another country. Oval Office (about 23:41): USAID gave poor value.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Says climate change is real, left advisory councils over the Paris withdrawal and pushed a carbon tax; also criticizes many regulations.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: At Tesla's September 2022 AI Day he said humanoid robots mean 'a future of abundance, a future where there is no poverty' (Isaacson, chapter 'Optimus Unveiled'); he also calls AI a leading existential risk.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Called nuclear shutdowns madness and urged keeping plants running and restarting closed ones.

experts-over-public.rationale: Oval Office (Feb 2025, about 1:35-2:20): wants elected representatives, not an unelected bureaucracy, to decide.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Re-sourced to his own post (rules 4): in June 2018 he wrote that a higher estate tax is better than income or capital-gains tax because heirs are unlikely to be equally good at allocating capital.

reviewHistory.rationale: Has said he supports an estate tax because the chance that heirs are equally good at allocating capital is low.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Re-sourced to his own post (rules 4): in June 2018 he wrote that a higher estate tax is better than income or capital-gains tax because heirs are unlikely to be equally good at allocating capital.

basic-income.rationale: Has backed universal basic income since 2016 and in April 2026 urged 'universal high income' checks from the federal government to offset AI unemployment.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Said he wants a zero-tariff situation between Europe and North America and that he gave this advice to Trump.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Argued the government should not build charging stations (Isaacson, chapter 'Politics') and in June 2025 replied 'CUT IT ALL' to Trump's subsidy criticism, saying all subsidies should end.

direct-votes.rationale: Said Mars government should be a direct democracy where everyone votes on every issue; reported to support direct democracy generally.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rogan #2223 (about 2:05:05) and Rogan #2281 (about 42:47): people should succeed by hard work, talent and merit, not other factors; opposes DEI programmes. Lex #400 (about 1:55:26) opposes things that are anti-meritocratic.

limit-population.rationale: Calls population collapse a greater risk than global warming and promotes higher birth rates.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Mixed: pushed regulators to approve faster and builds rapidly (Isaacson, Starship chapters), yet called for AI oversight and signed the March 2023 letter urging a pause on large AI experiments.

human-enhancement.rationale: Record: in 2016 he founded Neuralink to implant brain chips that connect people directly to computers for 'human-machine symbiosis' (Isaacson, ch. 65 'Neuralink').

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Tucker Carlson 2023 (about 48:16-49:01): says governments could read unencrypted DMs, which is scary, and promises an encryption toggle so that not even X could read them.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Don Lemon interview (about 5:26): says he votes on issues rather than party and is independent in his thinking.

school-vouchers.rationale: In February 2025 he urged the Texas House to pass school choice, the bill giving families taxpayer-funded accounts for private school, saying children with only one bad school option never had a chance.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Said the America Party would focus on deficit reduction and fiscal conservatism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Rogan #2281 (about 1:04:14-1:05:01) and Oval Office (Feb 2025, about 20:37): argues that entitlements and free care for illegal aliens act as a magnet; says fraud money should at least go to Americans.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: After Russia invaded Ukraine he posted 'we need to increase oil & gas output immediately' (March 2022) and in Stavanger said oil and gas are needed in the short term and more exploration is warranted; he frames it as temporary.

elite-replacement.rationale: Wrote that the Biden administration was deliberately importing vast numbers of illegals for electoral gain; said no grand conspiracy was needed; framing is electoral, not replacement of natives, and critics tie it to replacement theory.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes the two parties as a failed 'uniparty' and launched the America Party in opposition.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Supports a carbon tax, AI regulation and basic income, beyond a minimal state, while seeking cuts to other functions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Rogan #2223 (about 2:05:05): wants individual liberties and opportunity regardless of race, religion or sex. Don Lemon interview: 'treat people like individuals'.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Oval Office (Feb 2025, about 0:48-1:35): argues democracy needs a feedback loop from the people to the government.

party-controls-media.rationale: His free speech stance and purchase of Twitter oppose government control of information.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: No stated position found on this statement.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Record: as DOGE head in February 2025 he moved to shut down USAID, the main US foreign-aid agency, folding what remained into the State Department (Bloomberg Government).

collective-defense.rationale: Endorsed leaving NATO, whose core is collective defense.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: His 2022 peace proposal would recognize Crimea as Russian and rerun referendums in occupied regions.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Told the Financial Times in October 2022 he would 'figure out a special administrative zone for Taiwan that is reasonably palatable'.

space-expansion.rationale: Record over words: he founded SpaceX in 2002 with the aim of making humanity multiplanetary by settling Mars, and has run it to that end since (Isaacson, ch. 14 'Mars').

reviewHistory.rationale: Founded SpaceX to colonize Mars and champions making humanity multi-planetary.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Said DEI is 'just another word for racism' and that racial discrimination is what DEI does.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rogan #2223 (about 28:04-29:38): organized a petition supporting the Constitution and defends the First and Second Amendments as limits on government.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Posted in October 2023 that having children 'should be incentivized, not be a financial penalty like it is in most countries', replying to Hungary's president on family benefits.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: In November 2023 he replied 'You have said the actual truth' to a post accusing Jewish communities of pushing hatred against whites; afterwards (DealBook, November 2023; Don Lemon interview, March 2024) he apologised, said no conspiracy is involved and that he is not antisemitic. The later position wins.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Called for a revenue-neutral carbon tax so polluters pay, calling the lack of one madness.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Joe Rogan #2223 (about 28:51-29:38): says the right to bear arms is there to protect against a tyrannical government, so citizens should keep their guns.

public-service-media.rationale: Posted 'Defund NPR. It should survive on its own.' in February 2025, rejecting public funding for the US public broadcaster.

voter-id.rationale: Backed the SAVE Act requiring proof of citizenship to register and said opponents were traitors.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Record: during Iran's 2022 protest blackouts he sought a sanctions exemption and SpaceX activated Starlink there, about 100 terminals by December, to bypass the government's cut-off.

prohibit-child-medical-transition.rationale: Posted in March 2023 that irreversible surgery or 'sterilizing drugs' should not be allowed until at least 18, and in April 2023 that any parent or doctor who does so should go to prison for life.

notes:
Views have shifted over time: he voted mostly Democratic and was socially liberal before 2022, then moved to Republican support. On many topics (healthcare, abortion, drugs, death penalty, tax levels) no firm recent position was found, so they are null. Many quotes come from outlets reporting his X posts; X posts were not read directly. The 2018 Mars direct-democracy remark and 2015 carbon-tax remark may not reflect current views. H-1B support (Wikipedia) was not scored because no statement matches.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 11 answers taken from it, 28 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.
